content: FHL1, also known as Four and a half LIM domains protein 1, is a protein in humans encoded by the FHL1 gene. LIM proteins are a specific class of proteins characterized by the presence of a highly conserved structural motif known as the LIM domain. This domain consists of a double zinc finger motif and is named after the proteins LIN11, ISL1, and MEC3, which were the first to be identified with this feature. FHL1 is predominantly expressed in skeletal and cardiac muscles. Its critical role in muscle function was highlighted in 2008 when researchers discovered that mutations or defects in the FHL1 gene are associated with a spectrum of muscle disorders resembling muscular dystrophy. These disorders range from severe, early-onset conditions in childhood to adult-onset diseases that share similarities with limb-girdle muscular dystrophy.
